Generalized Addictive Mixed Model

Source: vignettes/articles/gam.qmd

The package also includes gam(), which fits a generalized additive mixed effects model to tumor growth data. This model is useful when tumor growth over time follows a complex nonlinear trajectory that cannot be captured by polynomial terms.

By default, gam() fits the model:

\log(1 + \text{measure}) \sim \text{group} + s(\text{time},\ \text{by} = \text{group}) + (\text{time} \mid \text{id}) where s(\cdot) is a group-specific smooth term for time.

Model fit 

mel2 <- tumr(melanoma2, ID, Day, Volume, Treatment)
Warning:
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The time range is greater than 50, which may cause convergence
issues when fitting lmm(). Consider rescaling the time variable
to a larger unit (e.g., from days to weeks or months).
--------------------------------------------------------------------
fit <- gamFit(mel2)

Result summary 

summary(fit)

Plot 

plot_median(mel2) 
plot(fit, "predict") + ggplot2::scale_y_log10()
plot(fit, "contrast")
